name: Shackleton Crater
summary: 21 km crater at the south pole. Rim gets near-continuous sunlight, interior is a permanent cold trap that may hold ice.

name: Shackleton-de Gerlache connecting ridge
summary: Sunlit ridge joining Shackleton and de Gerlache craters. Top candidate for power and for reaching shadowed ice.

name: Mons Mouton
summary: Highland massif near the south pole with long sunlit periods and gentle slopes. Named Artemis III region.

name: Mons Mouton Plateau
summary: Flatter ground on the Mons Mouton massif, favoured for landing.

name: Peak Near Cabeus B
summary: Sunlit peak close to Cabeus, where LCROSS found water in a permanently shadowed crater.

name: Haworth
summary: Large polar crater with permanently shadowed floor, a candidate for water-ice access.

name: Malapert Massif
summary: Tall massif with direct line of sight to Earth, useful for communications.

name: Nobile Rim 1
summary: Rim of Nobile crater on the far side of the south pole, partly sunlit.

name: Nobile Rim 2
summary: Second landing area on the Nobile crater rim.

name: de Gerlache Rim 2
summary: Rim of de Gerlache crater, close to the Shackleton ridge.

name: Slater Plain
summary: Smooth plain near the pole, listed among the nine Artemis III regions.

name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
summary: First crewed landing, in basalt mare.

name: Apollo 12
summary: Precision landing near Surveyor 3 in Oceanus Procellarum.

name: Apollo 14 (Fra Mauro)
summary: Landing on the Fra Mauro formation, ejecta from the Imbrium basin.

name: Apollo 15 (Hadley-Apennine)
summary: First lunar rover mission, beside Hadley Rille.

name: Apollo 16 (Descartes)
summary: Highland landing in the Descartes region, reference for lunar highlands.

name: Apollo 17 (Taurus-Littrow)
summary: Valley between massifs with mare basalt and dark mantling deposits.

name: Luna 16
summary: First robotic sample return from another world.

name: Luna 20
summary: Sample return from highland terrain near Apollonius.

name: Luna 24
summary: Core sample from Mare Crisium.

name: Chang'e 3
summary: Rover on young mare basalt in Mare Imbrium.

name: Chang'e 4
summary: First landing on the far side, inside Von Karman crater.

name: Chang'e 5
summary: Sample return from young basalt in Oceanus Procellarum.

name: Chang'e 6
summary: First far-side sample return, South Pole-Aitken basin.

name: Marius Hills Pit
summary: 40 m deep skylight in a sinuous rille, possible entrance to a lava tube.

name: Mare Tranquillitatis Pit
summary: Deep pit near Apollo 11 with an overhanging wall. A candidate shelter site.

name: Mare Ingenii Pit
summary: Far-side pit in a swirl region with strong magnetic anomalies.

name: Lacus Mortis Pit
summary: Pit with a visible ramp from the rim to the floor.

name: Aristarchus plateau
summary: Volcanic plateau with pyroclastic deposits and a very young crater.

top_cells.name: Argentina, near Ojos del Salado and Laguna Negra

name: Gruithuisen domes
summary: Unusual silica-rich volcanic domes.

top_cells.name: Argentina, near Ojos del Salado and Laguna Negra
Chile, near Ojos del Salado and Laguna Negra

name: Reiner Gamma
summary: Bright swirl on a magnetic anomaly.

name: Schrödinger basin
summary: Well-preserved basin with pyroclastic deposits and a peak ring.

name: Rima Bode pyroclastics
summary: Dark mantling deposit with possible oxygen and metal resources.

name: Compton-Belkovich
summary: Thorium-rich silicic volcanic feature on the far side.

name: Ina
summary: D-shaped depression with very young-looking volcanic material.

name: Jezero Crater
summary: Ancient lake delta in a crater, explored for signs of past life and collecting samples.

name: Gale Crater
summary: Crater with a 5 km layered mound, showing a long record of wet and dry conditions.

name: Meridiani Planum
summary: Flat plain with hematite and sulfate rock, a classic dry, dusty Mars surface.

name: Gusev Crater
summary: Crater with basalt plains and the silica-rich Columbia Hills.

name: Oxia Planum
summary: Clay-rich plain chosen for the ExoMars rover to look for traces of life.

name: Elysium Planitia (InSight)
summary: Smooth flat plain where InSight listened to marsquakes.

name: Utopia Planitia (Viking 2)
summary: Northern plain with ice near the surface, landing site of Viking 2.

top_cells.name: Morocco, near Corona lava tube (Cueva de los Verdes)

name: Utopia Planitia (Zhurong)
summary: Southern Utopia plain explored by China's Zhurong rover.

name: Chryse Planitia (Viking 1)
summary: Large lowland at the end of giant outflow channels.

name: Ares Vallis (Pathfinder)
summary: Flood-carved valley with a mix of rocks.

name: Phoenix landing site (Green Valley)
summary: Polar plain where Phoenix dug up water ice a few centimetres down.

name: Arcadia Planitia shallow ice
summary: Plain with ice buried just below the surface, a candidate for water in a first base.

name: Deuteronilus Mensae
summary: Mid-latitude region with glacier-like flows covered by dust and likely rich in ice.

name: Mawrth Vallis
summary: Valley with a thick layered record of clays, a top science target.

name: Eberswalde crater
summary: Crater holding a well-preserved river delta.

name: Holden crater
summary: Crater with layered lake deposits and megabreccia.

name: Nili Fossae
summary: Trough system with carbonate and clay-bearing rocks.

name: Columbia Hills
summary: Hills inside Gusev with silica deposits that may be from hot springs.

name: Hebrus Valles
summary: Low-lying outflow-channel region near ice and lava, proposed as an exploration zone.

name: Arsia Mons skylights
summary: Deep pits on the flank of a giant volcano, possible entrances to lava tubes.

name: Noctis Landing
summary: Canyon-network region with water-related minerals, proposed for a crewed landing.

name: Erebus Montes
summary: Mid-latitude mountains with ice-rich flows.

name: Phlegra Montes
summary: Mid-latitude hills with glacier-like ice deposits.

name: Melas Chasma
summary: Deep central canyon of Valles Marineris with layered rock and sulfate minerals.

name: Hellas rim
summary: Edge of the deepest basin on Mars, where air pressure is highest.
